ambiguities.question: What does item (d)'s phrase 'two lift structures on the same R^m have vector fields in common' mean?
ambiguities.corroborated_by: balthasar (non-halting: logged the same soft spot as a [GAP], explicitly declined to halt, and reported no divergence in the cases it actually ran)
readings: A: same base field, different algebras -- same n, same f: R^n -> R^n, two Weil algebras A,B of equal dimension N; phi_m receives one prescription from f_A and one from f_B (Melchior reading II)
B: any common image, including degenerate elements -- some map F: R^m -> R^m lies in both lifted-image sets L(n,A) and L(n',B) (Melchior reading I / Casper reading A)
C: non-degenerate common image -- as B, but excluding the always-present degenerate/trivial common elements such as the zero field or scalar multiples of the identity (Casper reading B)

D: common refinement / compatible source -- h = f_A = g_B with the two identifications compatible with a common refinement of the two lift structures (Casper reading C; flagged by Casper as possibly near-circular, since it may assume the agreement it would be used to test)
witnesses: Casper: the zero field 0 on R^m is the A-lift of f=0 and the B-lift of g=0 for EVERY pair of lift structures on EVERY R^m -- so under reading B the hypothesis of (d) is universally satisfied and carries no information (near-vacuous), while under reading C it is a genuine restriction, and under D it plausibly forces agreement by construction (near-circular). Vacuous / substantive / near-circular is the full spread across readings B/C/D on the round's stated point of interest.

Melchior: n=1, N=3, m=3; A=R[e]/(e^3) basis (1,e,e^2), B=R[x,y]/(x,y)^2 basis (1,x,y); f(t)=t^2. f_A(a0,a1,a2)=(a0^2, 2a0a1, 2a0a2+a1^2), f_B(b0,b1,b2)=(b0^2, 2b0b1, 2b0b2) -- differ in the third coordinate by a1^2. Under reading B/C/D this pair is NOT an instance of (d)'s hypothesis at all (f_A != f_B as sets/images; f_A=g_B in standard bases forces f affine). Under reading A it IS an instance (same base field f=t^2, two algebras of the same dimension N=3), and the two prescriptions (f_A vs f_B) are independent, constraining phi_3 at two distinct arguments. Different verdicts on the exact case round 2's analysis ran.
